title: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill
what_it_is: Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (Amendment) Bill

sections.label: Port connectivity and Tuas terminal
sections.summary: The port provides global connectivity that drives the economy, so the Government invests in port infrastructure, including a new Tuas container terminal.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: More importantly, the port provides the global connectivity that drives our economy, helping to fuel the growth of sectors, such as logistics, manufacturing and wholesale trade.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Hence, the Government has made, and will continue to make, significant investments in developing port infrastructure; for instance, in the development of a new container terminal in Tuas with a capacity of up to 65 million Twenty-Foot Equivalent Units (TEUs).

sections.label: Notification and approval thresholds
sections.summary: Persons acquiring 5% or more of a designated entity must notify MPA, and those acquiring 25% or 50% or more, or disposing below 75% or 50%, need prior approval.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: First, any person acquiring interest that would result in the person holding 5% or more of the total interest in a designated entity will be required to notify MPA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Second, any person intending to acquire 25% or more, or 50% or more, of the total interest in a designated entity, will be required to obtain prior approval from MPA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Third, any person intending to dispose interest that would result in that person’s shareholding falling below 75% or 50% of the total interest in a designated entity will be required to obtain prior approval from MPA.

sections.label: New controller requirements
sections.summary: New part 12(a) imposes requirements for a 5% controller to notify authorities and for prior approval before becoming a 25%, 50% or 75% controller or indirect controller.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The new part 12(a) sets up new, detailed and onerous requirements, including an obligation for a person becoming a 5% controller of a designated entity to notify the authorities and a person needing to seek prior approval before becoming a 25% or 50% or 75% controller or an indirect controller of a designated entity.

sections.label: Proposed penalties under section 86(i)
sections.summary: The proposed punishments under section 86(i) include fines not exceeding $500,000 or $1,000,000 and imprisonment of three years, or both.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What is worse, in my view, is that under the proposed section 86(i), the proposed punishments, including fines, is not exceeding $500,000 or $1,000,000 and imprisonment of three years, or both fine and punishment, are very heavy penalties, indeed.

sections.label: MPA regulation of inland watercraft
sections.summary: The Bill has MPA take over from PUB the regulation of inland watercraft, including construction, maintenance, safe operation, navigation and crew manning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: What the Bill seeks to do is to have MPA regulate inland watercraft, a role which will be taken over from PUB.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under the new part 13A of this Bill, MPA will take over the regulatory roles relating to construction, maintenance, safe operation and navigation and the crew manning requirements and other aspects of inland craft.

sections.label: Engines for reservoir vessels
sections.summary: The Senior Minister of State is asked to clarify whether regulations on the use of engines for vessels in reservoirs are in the pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Minister of State clarify if any regulations on the use of engines for vessels in reservoirs are in the pipeline?

sections.label: Charging costs for vessels
sections.summary: Charging arrangements raise operating costs, with converting nine four-stroke vessels costing $300,000 to $400,000 and jetty charging facilities $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Any arrangement for such charging will invariably lead to higher operating costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: He added that changing nine vessels that are of four-stroke engines to battery or solar-powered ones will cost at least $300,000 to $400,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Installation of charging facilities at jetties, after obtaining the relevant permission from the authorities would cost another $50,000.

sections.label: Vessel identification in reservoirs
sections.summary: Vessels are easily identified in reservoirs because these water bodies are not large, prompting a request for the requirement's rationale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: They explained that vessels are easily identified in reservoirs since these water bodies are not large.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, can the Ministry clarify the rationale for this requirement for vessels in reservoirs or water bodies of similar sizes?

sections.label: Equity control requirements intention
sections.summary: Equity control requirements aim not to interfere with day-to-day operations or commercial flexibility but to require MPA approval for transactions crossing significant equity thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: The intention of the equity control requirements is not to interfere with the day-to-day operations of the designated entities or restrict its commercial flexibility, but rather to require MPA’s approval to be sought for transactions crossing stipulated significant thresholds in equity interest.

sections.label: Shareholder equity thresholds
sections.summary: A shareholder with over 25% equity interest can veto special resolutions, and one with over 50% can pass ordinary resolutions under the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: A shareholder who has more than 25% equity interest can veto special resolutions under the Companies Act.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: A shareholder with more than 50% equity interest can pass ordinary resolutions.

sections.label: MPA powers over shareholders
sections.summary: For the legislation to be effective, MPA must have powers over shareholders, positioning it to safeguard port interests and enhance reservoir and inland waterway safety.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: So, for the legislation to be effective, MPA must have the powers to go beyond just the public licensee to the shareholders as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
sentences.text: This Bill not only better positions MPA to safeguard our strategic port interests but also enhance the overall safety in reservoirs and inland waterways for all.
